messages.subject: reactivity question
parts:
Hello,

I have the following observer:

  observe({
    if(is.null(getBreaks())) return(NULL)
    bounds <- ratioTable()
    updateTextInput(session, "sub", value=attr(bounds,"run"))
  })

The two reactive functions getBreaks() and ratioTable() are not reactive to input$sub. However, whenever I modify input$sub in the interface, this observer is executed (thus I finally cannot modify input$sub).

But this problem is solved by isolating ratioTable() :

  observe({
    if(is.null(getBreaks())) return(NULL)
    bounds <- isolate(ratioTable())
    updateTextInput(session, "sub", value=attr(bounds,"run"))
  })

As I said, ratioTable() is not reactive to input$sub, but it is called by an output reactive to input$sub. Is it the cause of the reactivity of the observer ?

I have understand the mystery :)

This is due to the following piece of code:

    factors <- paste0("factor_", 1:nfactors)
    Factors <- unlist(reactiveValuesToList(input)[factors])

... which is reactive to every input ! 

Problem solved now:

    factors <- paste0("factor_", 1:nfactors)
    Factors <- isolate(unlist(reactiveValuesToList(input)[factors]))

messages.subject: Re: reactivity question
parts: On Mon, Nov 4, 2013 at 7:08 AM, Stéphane Laurent <lauren...@yahoo.fr> wrote:

I have understand the mystery :)

This is due to the following piece of code:

    factors <- paste0("factor_", 1:nfactors)
    Factors <- unlist(reactiveValuesToList(input)[factors])

... which is reactive to every input ! 

Problem solved now:

    factors <- paste0("factor_", 1:nfactors)
    Factors <- isolate(unlist(reactiveValuesToList(input)[factors]))

Yes, using reactiveValuesToList is discouraged for this very reason. In addition to "regular" input values, there are some input values that can change when you don't expect it, such as when the browser window is resized, and sometimes the hover position of the mouse over an image, so using reactiveValuesToList can result in your app doing way too much work. The function was previously called as.list.reactiveValues, but we renamed it to make it more difficult for people to turn the entire input object into a list and thus take a dependency on all input values.


At any rate, you might be better off with something like this:
factors <- paste0("factor_", 1:nfactors)

Factors <- unlist(lapply(factors, function(x) input[[x]]))

Or even better, use vapply (you may have to replace the `character(1)` with the the appropriate type):
vapply(factors, function(x) input[[x]], character(1))


-Winston
